_meta.tool: Plot Hole Finder (id: PlotHoleFinder, renamed from PlotHole 2026-09-06)
_meta.how_to_regression_diff: Re-run cases (npm run check:golden plot-hole — route slug unchanged, backend/routes/plot-hole.js was not renamed). Diff for QUALITY not exact match: HTTP 200, no truncation. FULL RENAME + V2 REWRITE (2026-09-06): id PlotHole -> PlotHoleFinder, URL /PlotHole -> /PlotHoleFinder with a real 301 (and /plothole, /plot-hole), TOOL_ALIASES entry, tool-og-slugs.json + og-slug-map.json new-id keys added alongside the old, localization-audit.js allowlist path updated. Deliberately KEPT the same: backend/routes/plot-hole.js filename and both endpoint paths (/api/plot-hole, /api/plot-hole/defend), the plh_* i18n prefix, and the plothole-result/plothole-history localStorage keys. The tool's actual behavior was also fully rewritten in the same pass: the old prompt forced 4-7 'holes' with a mix of severities regardless of evidence, and its PERSONALITY line asked it to defend the story 'like a skilled apologist' — which in practice meant inventing off-screen events, secret routes, and unseen assistance as established fact (e.g. 'Blake uses tunnels and abandoned infrastructure' for a method the film never shows), attributing generated one-liners to 'r/plotholes' as if they were real quotes, and asserting what 'nobody cares about' as though that were knowable. It also turned a character's motivated decision (Bane not killing Bruce immediately) into a 'MAJOR plot hole' while supplying — in the same response — the exact character-based explanation that makes it not a hole. FIND HOLES schema replaced: title_analyzed / overall_verdict{label,summary} / swiss_cheese_rating / swiss_cheese_note / focus_answer{show,question,verdict,explanation} / findings[]{name,type,severity,what_happens,case_against,best_defense,defense_basis,verdict,why,snarky_version} / strongest_case{show,finding,why} / what_the_story_gets_right{show,text} / why_it_still_works{show,text}. DEFEND schema replaced: hole_summary / defense_verdict / verdict_reason / defense_arguments[]{argument,basis,strength,support,counterpoint} / best_defense / closing_statement / final_call. NO FORCED QUOTA: findings/defense_arguments return only what survives scrutiny (usually 2-5 / 2-4), never a fixed count or a mandated mix of severities. TAXONOMY FIRST: each finding gets exactly one type (REAL CONTRADICTION / UNEXPLAINED GAP / PLOT CONVENIENCE / QUESTIONABLE DECISION / CONTINUITY ISSUE / TIMELINE PROBLEM / RULE-BREAK / NOT ACTUALLY A HOLE) before any verdict — severity (MINOR/MAJOR/STORY-BREAKING) is null for anything that isn't a genuine contradiction. FOCUS QUESTION: if the visitor points to a specific scene/decision/rule, it's answered first (focus_answer) before at most 1-3 other findings are added, rather than a scan of the whole work burying the visitor's actual question. SWISS CHEESE RATING KEPT (explicit decision, not an oversight — the supplied rewrite spec contradicted itself, saying both 'KEEP' with a worked example and, separately, to remove it; the schema/UI mock it also supplied omitted it entirely) — bare integer 1-10 under exactly that key name, the exact-key-name rule preserved from the pre-rewrite tool-notes lesson (a bare example alone once made the model rename the key to overall_swiss_cheese_rating and the rating silently stopped rendering). REDDIT QUOTES REMOVED: reddit_would_say -> snarky_version, an original joke never attributed to Reddit/fans/critics/viewers. WHY NOBODY CARES REMOVED (asserted unknowable audience psychology) -> why_it_still_works, framed as analysis of what the story accomplishes, never as claims about what viewers think. BIGGEST HOLE -> STRONGEST CASE, only shown when a genuine contradiction survives, not merely because it was the visitor's original complaint. Bumped both endpoints from MODELS.FAST to MODELS.SMART — sorting 'why didn't they just...?' from a genuine rule contradiction, and ESTABLISHED from STRETCH in a defense, is real reasoning work a fixed-quota version never had to do. Live-verified against the exact two examples the rewrite spec called out as broken in the old version: (1) Bane's delay in killing Bruce now resolves as focus_answer verdict 'NO — EXPLAINABLE' citing his established motive (wants Bruce to suffer, watch Gotham fall) instead of being logged as a MAJOR hole the response then explains away itself; (2) Bruce's return to blockaded Gotham now gets a REASONABLE-INFERENCE-labeled defense ('trusted intermediaries and institutional relationships likely still exist') with its own counterpoint noting the film never shows this, and a separate STRETCH-labeled argument explicitly self-flags 'This is fan-repair, not story logic' — no invented tunnels, contacts, or off-screen conversations stated as fact anywhere in either response. SECOND CORRECTION PASS (2026-09-06, same day): after live-testing, added 7 adjudication refinements. (1) A MORAL/ETHICAL CONTRADICTION IS NOT A LOGICAL ONE — new finding types THEMATIC TENSION, ETHICAL CONTRADICTION, QUESTIONABLE PREMISE added; a conflict between an institution's rules/ethics and a character's autonomy is not REAL CONTRADICTION unless two established facts about how the world operates genuinely can't both be true. (2) DO NOT DEMAND REAL-WORLD SCIENCE for an established fictional mechanism — ask whether the story uses its own rule consistently, not whether it explains the mechanism scientifically. (3) VERIFY BEFORE CLAIMING 'the story establishes' — both sides of a contradiction must be genuinely established, with weakening language ('the story appears to treat...') when uncertain. (4) UNRESOLVED MYSTERY added as its own finding type, distinct from UNEXPLAINED GAP, so an ongoing mystery-box series isn't penalized for not having revealed an answer yet. (5) Swiss Cheese Rating must be calculated only AFTER adjudication, weighted toward REAL CONTRADICTION/RULE-BREAK/TIMELINE PROBLEM/CONTINUITY ISSUE and away from gaps/conveniences/thematic findings, with an explicit consistency check ('would I still give this rating with only the surviving findings?'). (6) STRONGEST CASE now requires a YES — REAL HOLE verdict, not merely 'produced the most interesting discussion' — new hardest_question field (with its own icon/section, mutually exclusive with strongest_case) substitutes when nothing clears that bar. (7) DO NOT CLAIM DELIBERATE AUTHORIAL WITHHOLDING without evidence — 'the show is deliberately withholding...' replaced with 'the answer has not yet been revealed' framing. Live-verified with the exact example from the corrections: Severance's outie/innie consent question now resolves NOT A HOLE — DIFFERENT KIND OF STORY PROBLEM with explicit THEMATIC TENSION reasoning, and hardest_question correctly shows instead of strongest_case since no finding reached YES — REAL HOLE (see 'find-severance-outie-consent-is-thematic-tension-not-a-hole' below). 5 new i18n keys x 13 languages (95/95 parity).

cases.name: find-dark-knight-rises-bane-delay-focus-question
cases.why_this_case_exists: The exact example the rewrite spec called out: the old tool turned Bane's motivated choice not to kill Bruce immediately into a MAJOR plot hole while supplying the character-based explanation itself in the same response. This is the permanent regression guard for DO NOT CONFUSE 'WHY DIDN'T THEY JUST...?' WITH A PLOT HOLE.

input.title: The Dark Knight Rises
input.whatToLookAt: Bane captures Bruce Wayne but does not kill him immediately, instead sending him to a foreign prison pit. Why does Bane delay?

overall_verdict.label: A FEW REAL GAPS
overall_verdict.summary: The film is ambitious enough that its logic problems are mostly self-inflicted — it establishes rules and timelines it then quietly ignores. None of them collapse the story outright, but a couple leave genuine marks.

output.swiss_cheese_note: More convenience than contradiction. The big structural moves mostly hold; the holes cluster around the film's own stated rules rather than basic storytelling logic.

focus_answer.question: Why does Bane not simply kill Bruce Wayne after defeating him?
focus_answer.explanation: The film establishes Bane's motive clearly enough: he does not want Bruce to die quickly — he wants Bruce to suffer and watch Gotham fall first, from the one place he can see it happen with no hope of reaching it. Killing Bruce immediately would deny Bane that psychological payoff. That is a coherent, character-consistent motive, not a contrivance — the delay is the point.

findings.name: Bruce Wayne recovers from a broken back in what appears to be a few months, during a five-month siege
findings.what_happens: Bane snaps Bruce's vertebra; a fellow prisoner reduces the dislocation, and Bruce climbs out of the pit and returns to Gotham apparently in fighting shape well within the film's five-month siege window.
findings.case_against: Spinal injuries of that severity typically involve months of immobility before rehabilitation begins, let alone combat readiness, and the film does not account for the time compression.
findings.best_defense: The film never specifies how much of the five months is spent healing versus training, and Bruce is established across the trilogy as having extraordinary physical conditioning.
findings.verdict: NOT A HOLE — DIFFERENT KIND OF STORY PROBLEM
findings.why: The story doesn't contradict an established healing rule — it compresses a timeline in a way that strains credibility without technically breaking its own logic.
findings.snarky_version: The real superpower was the prison chiropractor.

findings.name: Bruce Wayne gets back into a sealed Gotham with no explanation
findings.what_happens: The film establishes Gotham under total blockade. Bruce escapes the pit overseas and simply appears in Gotham for the finale, with no shown or stated method of crossing the blockade.
findings.case_against: The blockade is the film's central physical constraint, trapping every other character — Bruce bypassing it without explanation undercuts the rule the story set up for itself.
findings.best_defense: The film may be implying the blockade isn't literally impenetrable to a sufficiently resourceful individual, and Bruce retains skills and contacts established over three films — the logistics may be deliberately elided for pacing.
findings.verdict: MAYBE — THE STORY LEAVES A GAP
findings.why: This is the strongest gap in the film — a hard constraint the story uses as a threat for everyone else, then silently exempts the protagonist from with no shown mechanism.
findings.snarky_version: Apparently 'billionaire ninja' is a sufficient travel document.

strongest_case.finding: Bruce Wayne re-enters a sealed Gotham with no explanation
strongest_case.why: This is the one place the film uses its own established rule — the total blockade — as a dramatic threat for every other character, then silently exempts the protagonist from it with no shown or stated mechanism.

what_the_story_gets_right.text: Bane's motive for keeping Bruce alive is one of the film's stronger pieces of internal logic — established early, consistent with his character throughout, and what makes the pit sequence more than an arbitrary detour.

why_it_still_works.text: Most of the gaps cluster around logistics rather than the film's emotional or thematic spine — the places where it skips a logistical beat are mostly not where the dramatic weight lands.

cases.name: defend-dark-knight-rises-gotham-return-no-invented-tunnels
cases.why_this_case_exists: The exact example the rewrite spec called out: the old tool's defense repeatedly turned speculative explanations into stated fact ('Blake uses tunnels and abandoned infrastructure' for a method the film never shows). This is the permanent regression guard for THE BEST DEFENSE never inventing unseen events, and for STRETCH-basis arguments never disguising themselves as ESTABLISHED.

input.title: The Dark Knight Rises
input.allegedHole: How does Bruce get from a foreign prison pit back into sealed Gotham with no money or ID?

output.hole_summary: After escaping the pit prison somewhere remote, Bruce is broke, unidentified, and outside a militarily quarantined city — yet he reappears in Gotham in costume with no explanation of how he crossed continents and a blockade.
output.verdict_reason: The logistics are genuinely unshown, but the film establishes no rule that makes them impossible — it simply compresses the journey entirely. The gap is real, but it is a compression, not a contradiction.

defense_arguments.argument: Bruce is one of the wealthiest and most connected people on Earth, and the film establishes that his resources were frozen, not destroyed — trusted intermediaries and institutional relationships likely still exist.
defense_arguments.support: The film shows Lucius Fox and Alfred as longtime associates with their own standing — a man of Wayne's stature likely has access to discreet channels without a formal paper trail.
defense_arguments.counterpoint: The film never actually shows any such contact being made, and earlier scenes suggest Bruce is genuinely cut off.

defense_arguments.argument: The quarantine of Gotham is enforced at the bridges and by threat of detonation — a deterrent aimed at the civilian population, not an airtight perimeter against a single covert infiltrator.
defense_arguments.support: The film shows Special Forces operatives being inserted into Gotham covertly, confirming the blockade has exploitable gaps for someone skilled and motivated.
defense_arguments.counterpoint: Those operatives had military logistics behind them; Bruce is doing this alone, from another continent, with no shown support infrastructure.

defense_arguments.argument: Bruce could have concealed a minimal emergency cache — cash, a contact, a stored identity — somewhere outside Gotham before the city was seized.
defense_arguments.support: Consistent with a character who plans for every contingency, but the film supplies no evidence of any such cache.
defense_arguments.counterpoint: This is fan-repair, not story logic — if the film wanted this to be the answer, it had ample opportunity to plant the detail.

output.best_defense: The strongest honest argument combines the first two: Bruce's global network of relationships didn't vanish when his bank account was frozen, and the Gotham blockade demonstrably has covert entry points. Neither fact is invented — both are in the film. Together they make the journey implausible to dramatize in full, not impossible within the story's world.
output.closing_statement: The prosecution is right that the film never shows the work. The defense contends it didn't need to — the story establishes who Bruce is, and who Bruce is makes the journey hard, not miraculous.
output.final_call: The gap is real, and the film earns some skepticism for leaning on a character's general competence to paper over an unresolved logistical sequence. But nothing the film explicitly establishes makes the journey impossible — it makes it unexplained. That's reduced charges, not a conviction.

cases.name: find-severance-outie-consent-is-thematic-tension-not-a-hole
cases.why_this_case_exists: The exact example from the second round of corrections: a conflict between a fictional institution's rules and a character's autonomy (the outie consents to severance, the innie does not) is the show's central ETHICAL problem, not a LOGICAL contradiction — both facts coexist fine under the story's own established system. Permanent regression guard for 'A MORAL OR ETHICAL CONTRADICTION IS NOT A LOGICAL ONE', for the new THEMATIC TENSION/ETHICAL CONTRADICTION/QUESTIONABLE PREMISE/UNRESOLVED MYSTERY finding types, and for hardest_question correctly substituting for strongest_case when nothing clears the YES — REAL HOLE bar.

input.title: Severance
input.whatToLookAt: The outie consents to severance but the innie never does. Is this a plot hole?

overall_verdict.label: MOSTLY HOLDS TOGETHER
overall_verdict.summary: Severance runs on deliberate mystery and institutional opacity, which gives it a lot of narrative cover. Most apparent holes dissolve into 'we don't know the rule yet' or 'the character doesn't know what the audience suspects.' A few genuine logic problems survive scrutiny, but they are outnumbered by things the show is either still building toward or has quietly accounted for.

output.swiss_cheese_note: One meaningful unexplained gap, one continuity wobble, one structural convenience the show leans on harder than it earns. The deliberate mystery-box construction makes it genuinely difficult to call something a contradiction when the show may simply not have revealed the relevant rule yet.

focus_answer.question: The outie consents to severance but the innie never does — is this a plot hole?
focus_answer.verdict: NOT A HOLE — DIFFERENT KIND OF STORY PROBLEM
focus_answer.explanation: Both facts coexist within the story's established system without contradiction. Lumon treats the outie's signature as legally and procedurally sufficient consent — the innie is not recognized as a separate legal entity capable of independent consent. That arrangement may be unjust and the show's central ethical provocation, but 'unjust' and 'internally contradictory' are different things. The story does not establish a rule that innie consent is required and then violate it; it establishes a system where innie consent is not required, and asks whether that system is monstrous. That is THEMATIC TENSION, not a plot hole.

findings.name: The Overtime Contingency lets innies surface anywhere — except when it doesn't
findings.what_happens: The Overtime Contingency is established as a procedure that can bring an innie to consciousness in the outside world. Lumon monitors severed employees extensively but does not appear to deploy this capability in every situation that seems to call for it.
findings.case_against: The show does not clearly establish what limits or costs apply to this capability — it appears or disappears according to what the plot needs rather than a clearly stated rule.
findings.best_defense: The show does not establish that Lumon treats this capability as routine; its selectivity could reflect constraints not yet explained rather than pure convenience.
findings.verdict: MAYBE — THE STORY LEAVES A GAP
findings.why: The capability is real within the story, but its rules and limits have not been established clearly enough to evaluate whether specific uses or non-uses are contradictions or simply unexplained choices.
findings.snarky_version: Lumon can beam an innie into a funeral but apparently can't be bothered to read the manual on when else that button works.

findings.name: Cobel lives next door to Mark — and this is never satisfactorily grounded
findings.what_happens: Ms. Cobel, Mark's direct supervisor, is also his neighbor Mrs. Selvig in disguise, observing him at home.
findings.case_against: The show does not explain how long this has been in place or how Cobel maintained two identities in close proximity without a slip.
findings.best_defense: Lumon's surveillance of severed employees is established throughout as extensive and institutionally normal — the implausibility functions as institutional excess rather than a violated rule.
findings.verdict: NOT A HOLE — DIFFERENT KIND OF STORY PROBLEM
findings.why: It is a significant convenience and a deliberately surreal choice, but the show does not establish a rule that this kind of surveillance is impossible — it establishes a world where this is exactly what Lumon does.
findings.snarky_version: Most HR managers just pull your badge logs. Cobel bought the house next door and learned to make casserole.

hardest_question.question: What, precisely, are the rules governing the Overtime Contingency — and does the show's selective deployment of it hold up once those rules are fully revealed?
hardest_question.why: Right now it reads as an unexplained gap — the show establishes that Lumon can trigger innie consciousness outside the building, but not when or why that capability is available. That absence of rules is the actual problem, not a contradiction within rules already stated.

what_the_story_gets_right.text: The show's institutional opacity is doing real narrative work, not just covering for lazy writing — establishing Lumon as a corporation that withholds information from virtually everyone earns a lot of ambiguity without it feeling like a cheat.

why_it_still_works.text: Severance is structured so that almost every apparent gap sits inside a larger unresolved mystery, which keeps the emotional and thematic machinery running even when a specific logical mechanism is unclear.
